govt_capex.evidence: Not applicable/not disclosed - no government capex-linked revenue exposure identified.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No specific floating-vs-fixed borrowings breakdown found; Divi's has historically operated as a low-debt/near debt-free company per credit rating commentary (CARE Ratings), so interest-rate exposure is likely small, but no percentage was disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Search snippets note raw material (solvent/petrochemical-linked) price inflation attributed partly to China's energy crisis and West Asia logistics disruptions, and that imports account for ~45% of raw material consumption, but no explicit % of raw materials that are crude-oil/petrochemical derived was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Third-party summary of a subsidiary annual report note states the group is 'affected by normal price risks, especially in the areas of aluminium procurement and energy,' consistent with Endurance's core products being aluminium/iron castings and machined components rather than petroleum/polymer-derived materials; no numeric % of crude-linked raw materials was disclosed in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Third-party excerpt of a subsidiary-companies annual report states the group 'has no currency hedges or other long-term supply contracts' (unverified against primary FY24-25 AR text).
inr_exposure.evidence: ~23.6% of FY25 consolidated revenue (~24% incl. other overseas) is generated by European subsidiaries (Italy/Germany, plus a smaller US-linked entity), implying meaningful EUR-denominated revenue/cost exposure at the consolidated level, though this is largely a natural hedge (local revenue vs local costs) rather than INR export receivables.

pli_scheme.evidence: Endurance Technologies did not appear among illustrative lists of PLI-Auto 'Component Champion' or 'Champion OEM' approved applicants found in public sources (e.g., Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, Tata Autocomp, Bosch, Lucas-TVS were named); the full approved-applicant list could not be independently cross-checked, so this is not a definitive confirmation of non-participation.

inr_exposure.evidence: International business (CDMO + international formulations combined) was ~₹1,649 crore of ~₹3,918 crore FY25 total revenue (~42%); domestic+CDMO combined reported at 69% of FY25 revenue (up from 55% in FY21), implying ~58% pure domestic formulations. Figures from company results coverage (Business Standard/press reports of FY25 results), no explicit hedging policy disclosure found.

Non-India revenue (US ~31% + Emerging Markets ~18% + Rest of World ~18%) totaled ~67% of FY25 consolidated revenue of ₹54,543.5 crore, per Sun Pharma's own Q4FY25/FY25 results press releases (sunpharma.com). US-dollar revenue specifically is clearest in the US segment (~31%); EM/ROW include mixed local-currency billing so this is a proxy, not a strict USD figure. No explicit hedging policy found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Secondary source suggested Sun Pharma is among companies 'approved' under India's pharma bulk-drug PLI scheme (alongside Cipla, Dr Reddy's, Glenmark, Wockhardt, Biocon), but this could not be corroborated against the official PLI beneficiary list or Sun Pharma's own AR text within the research budget, so left unconfirmed.

rural.evidence: Gabriel's OEM base is weighted toward 2-wheelers (e.g. Hero MotoCorp), where rural/semi-urban 2W demand is an industry-level driver; FY25 aftermarket business grew 7.3% YoY with deeper reach into B & C class towns per AR/press coverage, but no company-specific rural revenue % was disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Gabriel's railway business grew 16.5% in FY25, becoming the sole Indian-approved source for Vande Bharat shock absorbers plus a decade-long export contract with Siemens, indicating some government/infrastructure (Indian Railways)-linked revenue, but no % of revenue was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Auto component inputs include steel and rubber/petroleum-derived elastomers, generally margin-sensitive per industry commentary, but no Gabriel-specific raw-material-as-%-of-revenue or crude-linked figure was disclosed in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue reported around ₹110.6 crore in FY25 against total revenue of ~₹3,643-4,667 crore (standalone/consolidated), i.e. roughly 2-3% of revenue, implying limited direct USD/EUR exposure; no explicit hedging policy disclosed (source: trade press coverage of FY25 AR/results; figure not independently verified against primary AR text).

china_plus_one.evidence: Broker/analyst research notes describe Kajaria expanding its footprint in international markets (Middle East, Europe), with some framing this as capitalizing on 'China Plus One' global sourcing trends — but this appears to be third-party/analyst framing rather than an explicit company-disclosed narrative in the AR MD&A, and Kajaria remains overwhelmingly domestic-focused. No export percentages were confirmed.

rural.evidence: Multiple analyst notes describe Kajaria as having the widest reach in Tier 2/3 markets with strong penetration into semi-urban/rural India, citing volume growth driven by rising demand from Tier II-and-below towns; no specific revenue percentage tied to rural/tier towns was disclosed (source: broker research notes on FY25 results).

govt_capex.evidence: Sector-level commentary links the PMAY (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana) affordable-housing scheme's large outlay as a general tailwind for tile demand industry-wide, but no Kajaria-specific revenue linkage to government housing schemes was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: A regulatory 'large corporate' exemption filing reportedly noted Kajaria had zero/minimal long-term debt on a standalone basis, suggesting limited direct floating-rate liability exposure on its own balance sheet, though end-customer housing/real-estate demand is broadly interest-rate sensitive. No explicit MD&A interest-rate disclosure was located.

crude_exposure.evidence: Kajaria's primary energy input for kiln firing is natural gas (LNG/propane), not crude oil. Third-party estimates put power & fuel costs around ~20% of FY25 revenue, but this is not a crude-oil-linked raw material figure and is sourced from broker estimates rather than the company's own AR disclosure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are described as a small and declining share of revenue (industry-wide tile exports fell ~20% in FY25 amid Red Sea shipping disruptions), but no Kajaria-specific USD revenue percentage or hedging policy was found; some indirect forex exposure likely exists via imported LNG/natural gas.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India's CY2024 results commentary describes a 'supportive domestic macro environment with strong traction from government-backed sectors such as transportation, manufacturing, data centers, electrification, renewables, and digitalization,' citing project wins including electrification for the Mumbai-Pune highway link, Dwarka Expressway, Varanasi ropeway, Zozila tunnel; motors for the government's Jal-Jeevan Mission; and traction motors for metro rail projects in three Indian cities. inr_exposure.evidence: ABB India's CY2024 revenue grew ~17% YoY to approximately ₹12,188-12,542 crore, with exports reportedly growing 33% YoY per company news releases, suggesting rising export/forex exposure, but no % of revenue figure or hedging policy was found in accessible sources (primary AR PDF inaccessible - HTTP 403).

Revenue mix reported (via secondary equity-research aggregation, not directly confirmed from AR PDF text) as roughly India 55%, Brazil 10%, US 10%, Germany 10%, Other markets 15%. Exact USD-denominated revenue % and hedging policy not found; note Brazil/Germany revenue is BRL/EUR-denominated, not purely USD, so a single USD-exposure figure would be misleading.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative found or expected; OFSS is a banking software products/IT services company, not a manufacturer, so this signal is not applicable.

inr_exposure.evidence: Could not access readable primary MD&A text (direct PDF fetches to screener.in/bseindia.com returned 403; an oracle.com-hosted AR 2023-24 PDF was retrieved but was binary/unparseable).
